gnarl: A knot in wood; a knurl or a protuberance with twisted grain, on a tree.
gnarlier: comparative form of gnarly: more gnarly
gnarliest: superlative form of gnarly: most gnarly
gnarling: present participle and gerund of gnarl
gnarly: Having or characterized by gnarls; gnarled.
gnarred: simple past and past participle of gnar
gnarring: present participle and gerund of gnar
gnarrs: third-person singular simple present indicative of gnarr
gnash: To grind (one's teeth) in pain or in anger.
gnashed: simple past and past participle of gnash
gnashes: third-person singular simple present indicative of gnash
gnashing: The action of something that is gnashed.
gnat: A biting insect, especially a mosquito.
gnatcatcher: A member of any of various species of small passerine birds in the family Polioptilidae found in North America and South America, close relatives of the wrens.
gnathic: Of or pertaining to the jaw.
gnathion: A craniometric point, being the lowest part of the middle line of the mandible.
gnathite: Any of the mouth appendages of the Arthropoda.
gnatlike: Resembling or characteristic of a gnat; tiny, insignificant.
gnaw: To bite something persistently, especially something tough.
gnawed: simple past and past participle of gnaw
gnaws: third-person singular simple present indicative of gnaw
gneiss: A common and widely-distributed metamorphic rock having bands or veins, but not schistose.
gneissoid: Having a structure similar to that of gneiss, or intermediate between that of gneiss and mica or granite
gnocchi: Italian pasta-like dumpling(s) made of potato or semolina.
gnome: An elemental (spirit or corporeal creature associated with a classical element) associated with earth.
gnomic: Of, or relating to gnomes (sententious sayings).
gnomon: An object such as a pillar or a rod that is used to tell time by the shadow it casts when the sun shines on it, especially the pointer on a sundial.
gnomonic: Showing all great circles as straight lines, and thus preserving the shortest distances between any two locations.
gnosis: An immanent form of knowledge or transcendent insight, such as sought by the Gnostics.
gnotobiotically: In terms of, or by means of, gnotobiotics.
gnu: A large antelope of the genus Connochaetes, native to Africa, having curved horns.
